title: Nuclear Energy Regulatory Overcaution
bottleneck: Nuclear regulation prices risk as if any release were catastrophic, making new reactors uneconomical in the West despite nuclear's strong safety record relative to fossil fuels. Licensing timelines stretch a decade or more, and regulatory ratcheting adds costs without proportional safety gains. Public fear, amplified by rare accidents, sustains political pressure for ever-tighter rules regardless of comparative risk.
why_it_blocks: Overcautious nuclear regulation keeps carbon-free baseload power off the grid, slowing decarbonization. Climate goals slip further out of reach with each decade of delayed deployment.
current_state: Advanced reactor licensing reform is underway in the US, but no redesigned regulatory paradigm is yet proven at deployment scale. Risk-informed, technology-neutral licensing could unlock deployment but faces entrenched opposition. A technology-neutral, risk-informed framework would serve both safety and climate goals.
